question: What protection is claimed for the body such that poison does not enter it, even in the case of being bitten by great serpents?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Even in that case, poison does not enter the body.
The negation applies to entry of poison into the body.
inference: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
uncertainties: The source of this protection is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
